title: Know your beads, strings and tools before you start

say: Know your beads, strings and tools before you start.
This is the video for module one of Bead Making and Simple Crafts: materials, tools and a safe workspace.
To make pieces people will buy, first understand the beads themselves.

say: Most beads are measured in millimetres across the widest part.

panel.heading: How beads are measured and sold
items: Most beads: millimetres across the widest part
4 mm is a peppercorn, 8 mm is a chickpea
Seed beads: 11/0, bigger number, smaller bead

say: A 4 mm bead is about the size of a peppercorn. An 8 mm bead is about the size of a chickpea.

say: Seed beads, the tiny ones, use the aught size, written like 11/0. Say it eleven aught. Here the bigger the number, the smaller the bead.

say: Many round beads come on a strand of about 40 cm. To guess the count, divide 400 by the bead size in mm. So about 100 beads of 4 mm, or 50 beads of 8 mm.

say: Step four. Add about 10% spare for faulty or chipped beads.
And before you buy, check that your wire or thread can pass through the hole twice. Carry a short piece of your wire to the shop and test a bead.

say: Beading wire is tiny steel wires twisted together and coated in nylon. It lasts longer and holds heavy beads. You finish it with crimps and crimping pliers.
More strands inside, such as 49, means a softer drape. Use the thickest wire that still passes through your beads twice.

panel.heading: Wire or elastic for a bracelet?

say: Elastic cord is fast and cheap and needs no clasp, but it can stretch out over time. Use it for light beads, finished with a surgeon's knot and a dot of glue.
Do not use sewing thread. It frays and snaps under the weight of glass beads.

panel.heading: Wire or elastic for a bracelet?

say: Flush cutters cut beading wire and head pins with a flat, neat end.

say: Beads, crimps and jump rings are choking hazards. Keep containers closed and out of reach of young children, and sweep the floor after work. Never make bead necklaces for babies or toddlers.

cards.d: Beads and crimps are choking hazards. Keep boxes closed and never make bead necklaces for babies.
Cut wire pointing down into a bag or your palm. Wear glasses when cutting.
Sit at a table in good light. Every 20 minutes, look far away for 20 seconds.

say: Cut wire pointing down into a bag or your palm, because short ends can fly off. Wear ordinary glasses or safety glasses.

say: Sit at a table, not on the floor or bed, with good light. Every 20 minutes, look at something about 20 feet away for 20 seconds, and stand up and stretch every hour.

say: To remember. Start with glass and crystal-style beads. Read sizes in millimetres, and aught sizes for seed beads. Count your beads and add 10% spare. Use crimps for wire and a knot for elastic. And keep small parts away from children.

say: Now practise. Make a bead reference card with five labelled beads, write your starter findings list with approximate prices, set up your workspace, and measure three wrists. For a bracelet, add 1.5 to 2.5 cm to the wrist measurement.
